title: Cap. VI Arg. 7 close: then Peter no more ordained than Judas — fights Eph. 1:4 and Acts 13:48
pass_a_gloss: If these things were so, there would be no difference between the elect and the passed-by from Divine operation, but only from human; nor would Peter have been more ordained by God to eternal life than Judas: but because by believing and persevering he satisfied this universal decree, Whosoever shall have perseveringly believed shall be saved, but Judas did not satisfy, therefore this one was received into the number of the elect, that one excluded from the same number. But all these things are plainly absurd and fighting with the Scriptures, which teach that certain ones were elected in Christ before the foundations of the world were laid, that they might be holy and blameless, Eph. 1:4. That certain ones were gifted with faith before others, because before others they were ordained by God from mere mercy to life; as Matt. 11:25-26; Acts 13:48; John 6:37; and elsewhere throughout.
pass_b_english: If so, elect and passed-by would differ only by human operation, not divine — and Peter would be no more ordained by God to eternal life than Judas. Peter would enter the elect number only because he met the universal decree Whoever perseveringly believes shall be saved; Judas failed it and was shut out. Plainly absurd, and at war with Scripture: some elected in Christ before the world's foundation, to be holy and blameless (Eph. 1:4); some gifted with faith before others because before others God from mere mercy ordained them to life — Matt. 11:25-26; Acts 13:48; John 6:37; and throughout.
source_text: Haec si ita essent, nulla esset differentia inter electos et praeteritos ex Divina operatione, sed solummodo ex humana; nec Petrus a Deo magis ordinatus ad vitam aeternam fuisset quam Judas: sed quia credendo et perseverando satisfecit universali huic decreto, Quisquis perseveranter crediderit, salvus erit, Judas autem non satisfecit, ideo fuit hic in electorum numerum receptus, iste ab eodem numero exclusus. Sed haec omnia sunt plane absurda et cum Scripturis pugnantia, quae docent quosdam in Christo electos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, ut essent sancti et inculpati, Eph. i. 4. Quosdam prae aliis fide donatos, quia prae aliis fuerunt a Deo ex mera misericordia ad vitam ordinati; ut Matth. xi. 25, 26; Act. xiii. 48; Joh. vi. 37; et alibi passim.
